_strings.@@9b76166b72d2: Renter's and Homeowner's School Property Tax Credit — Wisconsin filers who paid rent during 2025 for living quarters used as their principal home, OR who paid property taxes during 2025 on their home. Available whether or not the homestead credit is claimed. Cannot be claimed if you or your spouse claim the veterans and surviving spouses property tax credit. Rent for property-tax-exempt housing (e.g. university dorms, nonprofit senior housing, certain public housing) does not qualify.
_strings.@@9cd987bfb5f5: Treaty conformity — WI conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from WI income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the WI return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Wisconsin Form 1 starts from federal adjusted gross income (2025 Form 1, Line 1; the instructions direct the filer to fill in federal AGI from line 11 of federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR). Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and is never added back on the Wisconsin return. The 2025 Schedule AD (Additions to Income) instructions enumerate every addition modification — state and municipal interest, the capital gain/loss addition, nonqualified Edvest/Tomorrow's Scholar and ABLE distributions, the federal NOL deduction, lump-sum distributions (federal Form 4972), PFIC excess distributions, related-entity expenses, expenses for moving a business outside Wisconsin or the U.S., federal/Wisconsin basis differences, marital-property reporting differences, farmland-preservation and other computed-credit addbacks, tax-option (S) corporation and partnership entity-level adjustments, and other additions — and NONE adds back income exempt under a U.S. tax treaty. Form 1 Line 2 (additions via Schedule I) only converts for federal-law provisions Wisconsin has not adopted, not treaties. Therefore treaty-exempt income flows through and is NOT re-taxed -> conforms = true. (No explicit treaty provision text was found at the DOR, so this is flagged in unverified.)
_strings.@@a3a9f3e72f50: Wisconsin Homestead Credit (property-tax / rent circuit-breaker) — Per the 2025 Form 1 instructions Special Instructions: at least 18 years old on December 31, 2025; if under age 62 and not disabled, must have earned income; a legal resident of Wisconsin for all of 2025; not claimed as a dependent on anyone's 2025 federal return (unless 62 or older on December 31, 2025); not living in tax-exempt public housing for all of 2025 (exceptions apply); not living in a nursing home and receiving medical assistance (Title XIX) when filing; and not claiming (self or spouse) the veterans and surviving spouses property tax credit or farmland preservation credit. Claimed on Schedule H (or the simpler Schedule H-EZ).
_strings.@@a50bff30da8e: Wisconsin Earned Income Credit (EITC) — Full-year Wisconsin resident who qualifies for the federal earned income credit AND has at least one qualifying child (the federal definition of qualifying child applies). A married-filing-separate filer is ineligible unless they meet sec. 7703(b), IRC (in which case the Wisconsin filing status should be head of household, married). 'Federal earned income credit' means the credit computed using the IRC as adopted by Wisconsin — filers with Schedule I Part I adjustments recompute it on Schedule I Part III. A copy of federal Schedule EIC must be included (and federal Form 8867 if a paid preparer was used).

The 2025 Tax Rate Schedules on page 3 have been updated to reflect that change.' The 4.4% band now runs to $50,480 for single/head of household (2024: $28,640), $67,300 for married filing jointly (2024: $38,190), and $33,650 for married filing separately (2024: $19,090) — an increase of roughly 76% in each case, far beyond inflation indexation. The first-bracket tops moved only by indexation ($14,320 -> $14,680; $19,090 -> $19,580; $9,550 -> $9,790) and the 5.3%/7.65% crossover also re-indexed ($315,310 -> $323,290; $420,420 -> $431,060; $210,210 -> $215,530). The four rates 3.5% / 4.4% / 5.3% / 7.65% are UNCHANGED. Base guidance: Supply 2025 Wisconsin Form 1, Line 11 ('Subtract line 10c from line 9. If line 10c is larger than line 9, fill in 0. This is taxable income'). Line 11 = Wisconsin income (Line 7) minus the sliding-scale standard deduction (Line 8, from the 2025 Standard Deduction Table, p.35) minus Line 10c exemptions ($700 x exemptions on Line 10a + $250 x age-65 checkboxes on Line 10b). Those deductions/exemptions must be computed on the form BEFORE supplying the base — this pack ships no standard deduction and no exemptions, so nothing is re-subtracted here. SOURCE ASSEMBLY: the 2025 Form 1 booklet prints no single four-bracket rate schedule. Brackets 1-2 (rates and dollar boundaries $14,680/$50,480 single-HoH, $19,580/$67,300 MFJ, $9,790/$33,650 MFS) are from the 2025 Form 1-ES '2025 Tax Rate Schedules for Full-Year Residents'; brackets 3-4 (5.3% up to $323,290/$431,060/$215,530, then 7.65%) are corroborated by the Form 1 p.44 Tax Computation Worksheet. Cross-check: every worksheet subtraction constant equals the cumulative sum of the prior brackets — Single/HoH $586.44 exact and $8,183.76 vs exact $8,183.755; MFJ $781.92 and $10,911.83 both exact; MFS $390.96 exact and $5,455.92 vs exact $5,455.915 — and every 1-ES gross-tax constant ($513.80/$2,089.00/$16,547.93; $685.30/$2,784.98/$22,064.26; $342.65/$1,392.49/$11,032.13) equals the cumulative marginal sum exactly. Max divergence $0.005 (cent rounding), immaterial. Schedule C (MFS) is exactly half Schedule B (MFJ) at every bound. TABLE MANDATE below $100,000 — Form 1 Line 12 requires the Tax Table (instructions pp.38-43) when Line 11 is under $100,000; the table computes tax at the MIDPOINT of each income band (spot-verified: the $15,900-$16,000 row prints Single/HoH $570, MFJ $558, MFS $614, which reproduce from midpoint $15,950 as $569.68 / $558.25 / $613.69), so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within a table band and the filed form must use the table. At $100,000 or more the mandated Tax Computation Worksheet IS exact bracket math (identical to this pack, to within the half-cent constant rounding above). STANDARD DEDUCTION NOT SHIPPED (income-dependent): Wisconsin's standard deduction is a sliding amount from the 2025 Standard Deduction Table (p.35) based on Line 7 income — maximums $13,560 single / $25,110 married filing jointly / $11,930 married filing separately / $17,520 head of household, phasing to $0 as income rises (per the 2025 Form 1-ES schedules: single $13,560 less 12% of income over $19,550, zero above $132,549; MFJ $25,110 less 19.778% of income over $28,210, zero above $155,169; MFS $11,930 less 19.778% of income over $13,390, zero above $73,709; head of household $17,520 less 22.515% of income over $19,550 up to $57,210, then the single formula, zero above $132,549). Filers claimable as a dependent use the Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependents (greater of $1,350 or earned income plus $450, capped at the table amount); short-period filers and federal Form 4563 filers get $0. Compute it on Form 1 Line 8 — the supplied Line 11 base is already net of it. EXEMPTIONS NOT SHIPPED (already inside the Line 11 base): Wisconsin's exemptions ARE base reductions — $700 per exemption on Line 10a (taxpayer, spouse, and each dependent listed on federal Form 1040/1040-SR; 0 exemptions for a filer claimable as a dependent on another return) plus $250 on Line 10b for taxpayer and/or spouse 65 or older on December 31, 2025 (only if allowed the $700 on Line 10a) — but they are subtracted on the form in arriving at Line 11, so this pack ships none; do NOT re-subtract them from the supplied base. Head of household uses the SAME rate schedule as single (2025 Tax Computation Worksheet Section A 'Single or Head of household'; 2025 Form 1-ES Schedule A 'Single, Head of Household, Estates and Trusts'). Estates and trusts (fiduciaries) also use this schedule. QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE — the engine's default mapping is WRONG for Wisconsin: Wisconsin has no QSS status; per the 2025 Form 1 instructions, 'If you file your federal return as a qualifying surviving spouse, you may file your Wisconsin return as head of household.' A federal QSS must therefore be passed as head_of_household here, NOT married_filing_jointly. (A taxpayer whose spouse died during 2025 may still file 2025 as married filing jointly.) FULL-YEAR RESIDENT Form 1 ONLY: nonresidents and part-year residents file Form 1NPR and must PRORATE the tax brackets by the ratio of Wisconsin income to federal adjusted gross income — the 2025 Form 1-ES instructions print the rule with a worked example ('for a single individual the tax brackets are $14,680, $35,800, and $272,810. Assuming the individual has a ratio of 20%, the first $2,936 ($14,680 x .20) is taxed at 3.5%, the next $7,160 ($35,800 x .20) is taxed at 4.4%, and the next $54,562 ($272,810 x .20) is taxed at 5.3%. Taxable income over $64,658 ($323,290 x .20) is taxed at 7.65%.'). Applying these brackets unprorated to a 1NPR filer is wrong. The standard deduction and exemptions must be prorated by the same ratio. Credits taken after Line 12 are NOT modeled (they are subtracted from tax, not from income): itemized deduction credit (Line 13, Schedule 1), additional child and dependent care credit (Line 14, Schedule WI-2441), blind worker transportation services credit (Line 15 — the 2025 face prints 'Qualifying expenses .00 x 50% = 15' and the instructions a 'credit for 50% of the expenses paid. The credit may not exceed $1,500 ($3,000 of expenses) per qualifying person'), school property tax credit (Line 16, max $300 / $150), Working Families Tax Credit (Line 17 — the 2025 instructions say 'Do not enter any amount on this line. No credit is allowable for any individual or couple filing this form, since any taxpayer(s) who would qualify will not have a tax to offset.'), married couple credit (Line 18, Schedule 2, 3% of up to $16,000, max $480), earned income credit (Line 30, 4% / 11% / 34% of the federal EIC), homestead credit (Line 33, Schedule H), and the other Form 1 credits. Line 25 'Penalties on IRAs, retirement plans, MSAs, etc.' adds 33% of the federal penalty to the tax: the 2025 face prints '.00 x .33 = 25' and the instructions say 'Multiply the amount filled in by .33 (33%)' — not modeled (it is added after Line 12, like the credits above). The 2025 Form 1 face and instructions cite federal AGI as 'line 11 of federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR'; the TY2025 federal Form 1040 prints AGI on line 11a (formpacks/federal/2025/f1040 keys it 11a and the WI pack's cross_form binds f1040.11a) — the DOR's wording lags the federal form, the amount is the same. 2025 subtraction changes affect the BASE the caller supplies, not this schedule (2025 Form 1 instructions, 'New in 2025'): a new retirement-income subtraction of up to $24,000 for individuals at least 67 years old at the end of 2025; the college savings account subtraction increased to $5,130 per beneficiary ($2,560 if married filing separately); the tuition and fee expenses subtraction increased to $7,649 per student with a wider phase-out; and the adoption expenses subtraction increased to $15,000 per child. Compute these on Schedule SB / Schedule CS before supplying Line 11.
